validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, active FERC proceeding. Texas Eastern Transmission, LP (a subsidiary of Enbridge) filed FERC Docket No. CP25-491-000 on 5/15/2025 for the Appalachia to Market III Project (federalregister.gov 2025-09918, 90 FR 23327); FERC issued the Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity 2/25/2026 (EIA Aug2026 release, sheet 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects', row 9; Thompson Energy Expert trade report, headlined 'Texas Eastern Granted Authorization for A2M III Project'); construction begins March 2027, in-service August 2027 (EIA; Enbridge project page). CLASSIFICATION: correctly classed transmission/gas — an interstate NGA section 7(c) certificate for TETCO's Line 1 mainline, EIA Pipeline Type='Interstate'. DUPLICATE: not a duplicate of any of the other 45 rows in this batch's roster (none is a TETCO Appalachia-to-Market phase). It IS one of a family of three TETCO 'Appalachia to Market' FERC dockets that the orchestrator should cross-check against P0260/P5832/P5835/P0261 in the northeast-alaska batch — see cross_row_leads for the other two phases' dockets/specs, each independently verified. This row (A2M III, CP25-491-000) is textually and numerically distinct from A2M (conversion, CP20-436, completed 2021-2022) and A2M II (CP22-486, under construction, in-service 2027) — different dockets, different scopes, different costs. TWO GENUINE DEFECTS FOUND on this row: (1) LengthKnown reads 0 mi despite Diameter=36in being populated — the project is NOT a compression-only scope, it physically relays ~2 miles of pipe (see spec concern below); (2) StartState/Province reads 'Delaware', which is wrong — Delaware is one of two LDC customers the expansion SERVES, not a physical facility location; every physical facility (the Line 1 pipe replacement and the Bedford Compressor Station) is in Pennsylvania (see attribution concern below).

validity.recommendation: Correct LengthKnown from 0 to approximately 2.0 mi (mi units, matching the already-populated Diameter=36in) — this project relays ~2 miles of pipe, it is not a compression/meter-only scope.
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's LengthKnown=0 with LengthKnownUnits=mi is internally inconsistent with the already-populated Diameter=36 (the ADDENDUM's own compression/meter-scope list flags this pairing as wrong). FERC's Federal Register notice of application (federalregister.gov 2025-09918, Docket CP25-491-000) states the project will '(i) take-up approximately 1.95 miles of 24-inch-diameter idled Line 1 pipeline in Adams and York counties, Pennsylvania and relay approximately 2.0 miles of 36-inch-diameter pipeline (Line 1 Pipeline) adjacent to and south of Texas Eastern's existing Line 2 pipeline.' EIA's Aug2026 release (sheet 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects', row 9) independently records Miles=2 for the same project. Enbridge's own project page also describes 'approximately 2 miles of 24-inch diameter pipeline' being replaced with 36-inch. This is a real, physical pipe-replacement (in the same corridor, larger diameter, not merely a compressor/meter upgrade), so LengthKnown=0 is wrong; it should read approximately 2.0 mi, consistent with the diameter already on the sheet.

validity.researcher_notes: Market-not-a-terminus defect (ADDENDUM route-vs-sheet guidance, rule 3). FERC's Federal Register notice of application states the Project 'will provide up to 32,000 dekatherms per day of additional firm natural gas transportation service from the Appalachian supply basin in southwest Pennsylvania to meet the needs of two existing local distribution company customers in Pennsylvania and Delaware' — Delaware names a DELIVERY CUSTOMER's state, not a physical facility. Every physical facility in the docket is in Pennsylvania: the ~2-mile Line 1 pipe replacement is in Adams and York counties, PA (western terminus at Texas Eastern's Bakers Watering Trough Valve Site, eastern terminus at a new receiver/crossover, both within the same Adams/York corridor per the notice), and the Bedford Compressor Station modification is in Bedford County, PA. Thompson Energy Expert's trade report independently paraphrases the same filing as 'facilities in Adams, York, and Bedford counties, Pennsylvania.' EIA's own Beg_State/End_State fields (DE, PA) appear to reflect the same customer-state conflation as the sheet — EIA is not treated as a corroborating source for the Delaware start-state here, precisely because the FERC filing it is compiled from contradicts it once read directly. I could not determine from the filing whether the Adams/York-county segment or the Bedford Compressor Station should map to GEM's 'Start' vs 'End' location fields specifically (the notice doesn't rank them geographically west-to-east beyond calling the pig-receiver ends of the Line 1 segment 'western' and 'eastern' termini within the Adams/York corridor itself) — leaving StartLocation/EndLocation county text unstaged rather than guess; a human editor should assign county-level detail from the docket exhibits. The state-level fix (both ends Pennsylvania, not Delaware) is solid.
